holidays.name: National Corn on the Cob Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate butter-slathered, salt-dusted, finger-licking corn on the cob. Expect messy chins and strands of corn silk stuck in your teeth, which is all part of the fun.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it was created informally by food enthusiasts and promoted through food calendars. It falls in early summer, when sweet corn starts appearing at farm stands and barbecues.
holidays.funFact: An average ear of corn has about 800 kernels arranged in 16 rows, and the number of rows is always even.

holidays.name: National German Chocolate Cake Day
holidays.description: A day for coconut-pecan frosted chocolate cake. Despite the name, there is nothing German about the cake except part of its name.
holidays.origin: The cake is named for Sam German, an English-American baker who developed a type of dark baking chocolate for Baker's Chocolate Company in 1852. A Texas homemaker's recipe for 'German's Chocolate Cake' was published in a Dallas newspaper in 1957, and the cake became hugely popular. The possessive was later dropped, which led to the confusion about its origin.
holidays.funFact: After the recipe was published in 1957, sales of Baker's German's Sweet Chocolate reportedly jumped dramatically, and the cake became a national sensation.

holidays.name: Kamehameha Day
holidays.description: A official Hawaiian state holiday honoring King Kamehameha the Great, who united the Hawaiian Islands. Celebrations feature parades, floral lei draping of statues, hula performances, and pageantry across the islands.
holidays.origin: Established in 1871 by Kamehameha V to honor his grandfather, who unified the islands into one kingdom in 1810. It remains one of Hawaii's most important official state holidays.
holidays.funFact: The famous King Kamehameha statue in Honolulu is draped with enormous flower leis, some of which are dozens of feet long, every year on this day.

holidays.name: World Pump Day
holidays.description: A day for pumping things, which is a more flexible concept than you might think. Pumps are the unsung heroes behind water supply, heating, and countless industrial processes.
holidays.origin: It was created by pump industry groups to raise awareness of how essential pumps are to modern life and to promote energy-efficient pump technology.
holidays.funFact: Pumps account for a huge share of the world's electricity use, with estimates often placing it near 10 percent, which is why efficiency is such a big deal in the industry.

holidays.name: Women Cops Day Celebration Observance: Kazoo Day Mashup (Unofficial Fun Day)
holidays.description: An unofficial day for celebrating silly buzzing instruments and goofy music-making. Gather friends and play whatever you can hum into.
holidays.origin: Quirky calendar sites and music enthusiasts grew a tradition of celebrating the kazoo, a simple instrument that dates back to 19th-century America.
holidays.funFact: The kazoo is a membrane instrument, so it only works when you hum or sing into it rather than blow, which makes it technically a voice modifier.
